svg.text: The round trip, against the mark that actually ships
Panel 1 is LOGO_MARK_D from src/components/logo-mark.ts — the outline the site draws. Panel 2 is the Illustrator objects the font was
measured from. Panels 3 and 4 are the font’s own glyphs rotated and scaled back into that frame. The white swash is not drawn.
LOGO_MARK_D, as the site draws it
the clipped ring shows as grey
1 vs 2 the shipping outline and the traced objects are the same drawing, but not the same file: aligned by bounding box they sit about
1 pt apart on a 100 pt mark, rising to 4 at the worst point. That is trace-against-production drift and it has never been checked before.
2 vs 3 the extraction is lossless where it claims to be: the O returns to within 0.011 pt of the ring’s fitted circle, and the A’s apex
and counter apex are exact. The only fringe is 0.83-0.89 pt at the feet, from levelling them.
2 vs 4 the grey standing proud is the ring clipped off on the legs’ outer edges — deliberate, and what stops the A being 847 wide.
Caveat on the 1 pt: panels 1 and 2 are aligned by fitting their bounding boxes, not by a common origin, so some of that gap may be the
fit rather than the drawings. Worth a proper look before anyone treats logo-mark.ts and the Illustrator source as interchangeable.
